IHSA State Series Proposal Analysis

Postseason Scenario Explorer: Separate Paths for Non-Boundaried Schools

Models the IHSA Competitive Balance Committee plan against the current system: all non-boundaried schools in a class — per the official IHSA list — get their own quadrant of the state-series bracket (2 of 8 sectionals), so a public school can't meet one before the state semifinals and exactly one non-boundaried school reaches each class's final four. The Current side of every sport uses actual IHSA sectional assignments and results. Click a sectional on either map, or use the filters.
More about the model & variants
Two custom variants are selectable under Separation basis: the same non-boundaried population with a custom number of separated paths merging at the Elite 8, and the legacy framing — private schools only, on their own sectional paths, unable to meet a public school before the super-sectional round. Current-side sectional assignments are each sport's most recently completed postseason (2026-27 for the fall sports, 2025-26 otherwise); regionals within them are modeled at the chosen size. The Proposed side is always modeled — that's the point of the exercise.

Bracket

Current shows the selected sectional's actual IHSA bracket — real seeds, matchups, and results from the most recently completed postseason (2026-27 for fall sports, 2025-26 otherwise). Proposed is always modeled.
How the brackets work
Where no real bracket is on file for a sectional, Current falls back to a modeled one. Modeled brackets seed by MaxPreps rating (see the Schools tab): the best-rated team plays the lowest seed, the next-best plays the next-lowest, and so on, keeping top-rated teams apart as long as possible. Only the first round shows matchups and projected travel, since this tool doesn't simulate results — later rounds show bracket structure only. Sports without rating data show a note instead. Respects the Scenario Explorer's Sub-sectionals toggle — when on, a modeled bracket's field splits into two independently-seeded halves that meet in one final.
Select a sectional to see its bracket.

Scenario overrides

Adjust a school's enrollment, toggle the 1.65× multiplier or success-factor class bump per sport, or move it to a different sectional — the Scenario Explorer and Full Data tabs reflect it immediately. Overrides live only in this browser (not saved or shared).
How the multiplier & success factor work
Reclassification uses IHSA's published enrollment cutoffs (current one-year cycle, ihsa.org/Schools/Enrollments-Classifications) for baseball, softball, boys/girls basketball, girls volleyball, and boys/girls soccer — the only sports this tool classifies by enrollment. These are two separate, independent mechanisms, and per IHSA policy both attach to non-boundaried status — private schools plus charters, magnets, and other schools without a geographic attendance area — not to private schools alone. The 1.65× multiplier applies to every non-boundaried program by default unless waived; the checkbox default comes from IHSA's own published waiver flag where one exists for the sport (see the IHSA-flag column on the Schools tab, all seven enrollment-classified sports in the current cycle), otherwise every non-boundaried program is assumed multiplied. Boundaried public schools aren't eligible and don't get the checkbox at all. The success factor is likewise non-boundaried-only: a direct one-class bump (e.g. 2A→3A) for a program that reached the state final 4 twice in the rolling three seasons before the one in question, independent of enrollment — IHSA's own published flag is the default where available (checkbox marked "(auto)"), falling back to a reconstruction from real state-tournament results back to 2022-23. Both are still editable per school if you want to explore a different assumption. Neither mechanism accounts for co-op programs, which classify on their combined enrollment rather than any one member's own figure — also flagged on the Schools tab where published. A Proposed-system move is only offered while the school is in the sport/class field currently selected above (that's what determines the path names available). Classification cutoffs and the multiplier value itself are edited from the Schools tab, since those apply sport-wide (or tool-wide) rather than to one school.

How the columns work
The IHSA-flag column (co-op host, multiplier waived/applies, success formula, played up) comes from IHSA's color-coded classification pages — current 2026-27 one-year cycle, all three season pages, so all seven enrollment-classified sports are covered. The multiplier and success-factor checkboxes are the same overrides as the Scenario Overrides tab, editable right here — defaulting to IHSA's flag where one exists (marked "auto") or a reconstruction from real state-tournament results back to 2022-23 otherwise. "Expected next year" projects the success-factor rule to next season's window, off this year's enrollment at the official 1.65× (ignoring any scenario overrides in effect) — a projection, not a guarantee, since it can't see next year's actual enrollment, tournament results, or flags.

Classification cutoffs

Drag or type a class's max-enrollment boundary to reclassify every school in the sport selected above at once — e.g. raise 1A's ceiling and see who moves into it. The top class is always "and over" and isn't editable.

Non-boundaried multiplier

The official multiplier is 1.65×, applied by default to every non-boundaried program (waivable per school/sport in Scenario Overrides). Changing it here models a different policy value across every sport and school at once — e.g. what would 1.5× or 2× do to classifications overall.

Class summary —

School list

Method: where actual IHSA assignments are unavailable, schools are grouped by recursive geographic bisection (balanced, contiguous splits), mirroring how sectional and regional boundaries are drawn; regional subdivisions are always modeled at the chosen size. Travel is one-way straight-line distance to the host site: the named IHSA sectional host where assignments are actual, otherwise the most centrally located member school (host schools travel 0). Any sectional's host can be reassigned from its roster panel — to another member, any IHSA school, or a custom venue by address (geocoded via OpenStreetMap). School locations are city-level ZIP centroids, so figures understate true road miles by roughly 15–25% and Chicago-to-Chicago trips read as zero. Committee plan fixes the separated side at 2 of 8 sectionals (one quadrant, merging at the state semifinals; sports named in the plan: football [not in this tool], boys/girls basketball, volleyball, baseball, softball, boys/girls soccer); custom modes instead recommend 8 × separated share of the field, rounded, kept between 1 and 4, merging at the Elite 8. Classes, flags and enrollments are the official 2026-27 one-year cycle (ihsa.org Enrollments & Classifications, pulled Nov 2026, all three season pages); real sectional assignments and brackets are each sport's most recently completed postseason — 2026-27 for the fall sports (boys soccer, girls volleyball, flag football; pulled Nov 2026), 2025-26 for the rest — so a winter/spring school whose class changed between cycles appears in its current class on the Proposed side while last season's real bracket stays in its old class. Girls volleyball's 2026-27 state-final results post after Nov 15 and aren't reflected in next-year success-factor projections yet. Non-boundaried status comes from the official IHSA non-boundaried schools list (source_data/ Non-Boundaried_Schools.xlsx); the 1.65× multiplier and success factor apply to non-boundaried programs (not just private), matching IHSA policy. Sources: 2026 girls flag football pairings; 2025–26 boys/girls lacrosse and boys volleyball assignments (Elgin and O'Fallon volleyball sectionals include sub-sectionals); 2024–25 water polo pairings. Charter and other non-boundaried public schools separate with the private schools except in the legacy private-only mode. Enrollment figures (Scenario Overrides tab) are each school's base ISBE-derived enrollment prior to any 1.65× success multiplier.
